problem: Embodied models are specialized to a single task family, robot embodiment or environment (manipulation vs. navigation, per-robot policies), so capabilities are fragmented and transfer poorly across tasks, environments and embodiments.
motivation: Manipulation, navigation and egocentric human motion look heterogeneous but share one structure: condition on vision, language and embodiment, then predict future actions or trajectories. A single generalist VLA that absorbs all these data could scale like general VLM pretraining and generalize better out of distribution.
key_idea: Build one VLA on Qwen3.5-4B with a DiT flow-matching action expert, treating manipulation, navigation waypoints and human hand motion as a shared padded action-and-trajectory prediction problem. Embodiment-aware text prompts specify the platform and control convention, and a four-stage recipe (T2A, CPT, SFT, RL) trains the model.
insight: A vision-free text-to-action stage installs a language-indexed action prior that helps downstream learning: SFT on Simpler-WidowX rises from 60.9% (no T2A) to 71.1% with T2A. The best mix is ~20% synthetic and 80% real data, with full-sequence prediction, Sigmoid-Normal timesteps, and 2k steps. Co-training with VL data helps on cluttered or compositional benchmarks (RoboCasa +4.9pp). Large-scale pretraining is what drives the real-robot and OOD gains: ALOHA average OOD success goes from 36.2% without pretraining to 76.9% with it. State conditioning gives only marginal gains (<=1.3pp), and RL in SimplerEnv alone transfers mildly to other benchmarks without forgetting.
method: Backbone + action expert: Qwen3.5-4B VLM plus a ~1.15B single-stream DiT (16 blocks) with AdaLN timestep conditioning, joint self-attention over VLM hidden states and noisy action chunk, trained with flow matching and a few Euler steps at inference.

Embodiment-aware prompt conditioning: a text template prepended to each sample gives robot tag, single/dual arm, waist/mobile base, control frequency and chunk size; this is the sole platform-specific interface, with no per-embodiment heads and no proprioceptive state.

Unified action/trajectory tensor: targets Y in R^{H x K} keep native control conventions (delta EEF, joint, dexterous-hand, VLN (dx,dy,dtheta), human wrist+10 eigengrasps). Values are zero-padded to K channels with a validity mask, per-dataset quantile normalization, and a per-channel masked loss.

Four-stage training: T2A (frozen VLM, DiT trained on text-only actions from 7.2M synthetic trajectories plus real data) -> CPT (joint training on the full mixture) -> multi-task SFT (VQA, grounding, manipulation, VLN) -> PPO RL with sparse success reward in SimplerEnv via RLinf (SDE conversion of flow-matching for log-probs, value head on VLM), giving Qwen-VLA-Instruct.

Pretraining mixture: 74.2% robot manipulation (>10k h public + >1k h in-house), 6% egocentric human, 7.5% navigation (instruction following, object search, tracking), 3.7% synthetic sim (RoboInF, 360k trajectories), plus VL data (general VL, 2D grounding, driving VQA, fine-grained action captions).
Navigation interface: VLN as waypoint prediction (8 waypoints per chunk) with a sliding-window waypoint action for VLN-CE; SFT keeps only successful episodes.
Multi-embodiment projection: a shared zero-padded MLP projection between DiT latent and action space, the lightest of three designs tested with similar accuracy.

setting.backbone: Qwen3.5-4B VLM + 1.15B DiT flow-matching action expert (fine-tuned end-to-end)
setting.training_data: Large-scale mix: >10k h public robot data (Bridge, DROID, AgiBot, RoboMIND, etc.), >1k h in-house, ~8M synthetic sim trajectories, egocentric human data (Ego4D, EPIC, EgoDex, EgoVerse, Xperience), navigation data, driving VQA, grounding, action captions, general VL; SFT on sim manipulation + VLN + VL; RL in SimplerEnv
setting.observation: monocular/multi-view RGB (ego + wrist cameras), language instruction, embodiment text prompt; no proprioception
setting.action_space: continuous action chunks via flow matching (16 steps for manipulation; 8 waypoints (dx,dy,dtheta) for VLN with sliding-window waypoint execution)
setting.simulator: LIBERO, SimplerEnv, RoboCasa-GR1, RoboTwin 2.0, DOMINO, VLN-CE (Habitat), IsaacLab for data

numbers.extra: Unified generalist trained jointly with manipulation and VL data; RL only in SimplerEnv
Base pretrained model evaluated on VLN-CE
Fine-tuned on in-house ALOHA teleop data

numbers.eval_set_note: 6 OOD tasks, fine-tuned on Bridge only

numbers_note: Manipulation benchmarks are not in the canonical list, so they are tagged as other:*. RoboTwin SR_Easy/SR_Hard are separate keys. T2A ablations are given only in figures with numbers quoted in text.
results: A single generalist, Qwen-VLA-Instruct, gets 97.9 on LIBERO, 73.7 on Simpler-WidowX, 86.1/87.2 on RoboTwin-Easy/Hard (beating ABot-M0 at 86.0/85.0) and 56.7 on RoboCasa-GR1. On VLN-CE it reaches R2R OSR 69.0 / SR 57.5 and RxR SR 59.6 / SPL 47.8, beating StreamVLN on SR. Zero-shot DOMINO SR is 26.6 (vs. LingBot-VA 24.1 and PUMA 17.2), and real ALOHA OOD averages 76.9 vs. 41.5 for pi0.5.
limitations: Embodied data is still small and narrow compared with VL data, so long-tail objects, contact-rich tasks and embodiments remain weak.
Joint training creates optimization trade-offs that can modestly regress pure VL and navigation performance.
Evaluations are mostly short-horizon and benchmark-driven; long-duration real-world deployment is untested, and R2R SPL/NE are not the best.
